p: The big roundabout at Old Street earned the nickname Silicon Roundabout thanks to the many tech companies and start-ups that sprang up around it, and the area still has a buzzing, creative energy. Old Street station, on the Northern line and with National Rail services, is right on the junction, so getting here is straightforward from most parts of London.

Before you head in, bring photo ID if you look young, as bar-led venues commonly check. Book a lane ahead, especially from Thursday onwards, and if there are more than six of you, consider two lanes to keep everyone involved. Swap teams halfway through to give the underdogs a fighting chance.

There's some fascinating history close by too. Bunhill Fields, a peaceful old burial ground just south of the roundabout, is the resting place of the poet William Blake, Robinson Crusoe author Daniel Defoe and John Bunyan, who wrote The Pilgrim's Progress. Across City Road, Wesley's Chapel is where John Wesley, the founder of Methodism, preached, and his house next door is open to visitors.

A little further south, the Barbican Centre is a brutalist landmark with a theatre, cinema, gallery and a hidden conservatory full of tropical plants. Hoxton Street, to the north, has its own market and a down-to-earth local feel. A great mix of old and new to pair with a few frames and a drink.
